title: Past-Due Payment Allowance at the Loss
content:
## Past-due payment allowance — Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda

Where a waiver's switch for past-due payments is on, the past-due payments on the GAP balance claim line are subtracted from the GAP balance only to the extent they exceed the past-due allowance. The allowance turns on the waiver's months in force at the loss.

| Months in force at the loss | Past-due allowance | Subtracted |
|---|---|---|
| 24 or more | 400.00 | past-due payments above 400.00 |
| 12 to 23 | 200.00 | past-due payments above 200.00 |
| fewer than 12 | none | all past-due payments |

**Months in force.** These are the whole calendar months from the waiver's sale date to the loss date on the claim line. A month counts each time the sale date's day of the month is reached. A loss date on an earlier day of the month does not complete the month, and there is no month-end adjustment.

**Where the switch is off.** No past-due payments are subtracted, whatever the allowance. The switch is on for every tier of the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda.

### Basis questions (hypothetical figures)

- *Waiver sold on 9 October of Year 1, loss on 8 October of Year 3, past-due payments 517.80.* That is 23 months in force, so the allowance is 200.00 and 317.80 is subtracted. With the loss on 9 October of Year 3 the waiver has 24 months in force, the allowance is 400.00 and 117.80 is subtracted.
- *Past-due payments of 186.00 with 15 months in force.* They are below the 200.00 allowance, so nothing is subtracted for them.
- *Past-due payments of 186.00 with 7 months in force.* There is no allowance, so the full 186.00 is subtracted.
